FLASHCARD SET · AGES 2 YEARS

Matching & Sorting flashcards.

Fifteen picture puzzles about how things go together: same, different, match this, sort that. There is nothing to write and nothing to get right on paper — your toddler points, you talk, and the thinking does the rest.

These cards belong to Toddler 4 on the Kiddo School learning path.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Talk through the answer

    Ask the question on the card, then wait. Whatever your toddler points at, say what you see: "you picked the apple — look, this one matches!" Talking about wrong answers teaches just as much.

  2. 02

    Play match with real things

    After the cups card, find two cups in the kitchen and put them side by side. Every card idea works twice as well with the real objects nearby.

  3. 03

    Cards on the floor

    Spread four or five cards out and let your toddler walk, crawl or flop next to them. Big movements plus big pictures keep wiggly two-year-olds in the game.

  4. 04

    One puzzle per sitting

    One card, one question, one or two minutes. These are thinking cards — they work best when your toddler is fresh, not tired.

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Same Balls Flashcard for Toddlers

      Two balls, exactly the same — the gentlest puzzle in the set. Your toddler's job is simply to notice that these two go together, and pointing counts as a full answer.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Shows two identical things side by side, so the eyes get an easy first win.

      Sort it for real

      Hunt the kitchen for two wooden spoons and hand both to the chef.

      What it teaches

      Spotting likeness, the seed of every matching and sorting game.

      Print it like this

      Card stock suits this one; balls get gripped hard.

      Tip for today

      Say same only when both are truly found, not before.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Matching and Sorting for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Same Apples Flashcard for Toddlers

      Two red apples, alike in every way that matters at two. This card quietly asks: can you spot when things are the same? — the first skill behind all matching games.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Practises careful comparing on a pair your child already knows by taste.

      Sort it for real

      Pair up the mittens on the radiator and press their palms together.

      What it teaches

      Close looking until alike is obvious without help.

      Print it like this

      Print two copies and keep one spare for snacking fingers.

      Tip for today

      One pair at a time; more just looks like noise.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Same Cups Flashcard for Toddlers

      Two cups that match, the kind your toddler stacks and clinks every day. Matching familiar objects is easier than matching new ones — that is why this card feels easy, and easy is fine.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Trains double-checking; a quick glance is not enough to call it same.

      Sort it for real

      Line the mugs up in pairs on the shelf, matching sizes as you go.

      What it teaches

      Confirming a match before declaring victory.

      Print it like this

      A home printer does fine; thick paper survives clattering stacks.

      Tip for today

      Match by size first; colour can wait for its own card.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Different Apple Banana Flashcard for Toddlers

      An apple and a banana sitting side by side — same family, very different fruit. This card starts the other half of the thinking: not just "same" but "different", and saying how.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Turns spotting differences into a game the fruit bowl can join.

      Sort it for real

      Hold up a banana and a breadstick and ask which one bends.

      What it teaches

      Noticing what sets two everyday things apart, feature by feature.

      Print it like this

      Choose normal paper; this card works best fresh from the printer.

      Tip for today

      Ask which is which before telling; wrong guesses are still thinking.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Different Animals Flashcard for Toddlers

      Two animals that are clearly not the same, even at a glance. The question underneath is the fun part: what makes them different? Feet, sound, size — every answer a toddler gives is a good one.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Stretches comparison beyond objects; two creatures could not be less alike.

      Sort it for real

      Sort the toy box into animals and wheeled things at tidy-up time.

      What it teaches

      Grouping living things apart from the rest of the toys.

      Print it like this

      Print at full size; the faces carry the whole game.

      Tip for today

      Let the mistake sit a second before helping; it often fixes itself.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Different Shapes Flashcard for Toddlers

      A circle and a square, side by side — one rolls, one does not. This card links straight back to the shape cards, and the difference has a built-in test any toddler can run: try to roll it.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Builds shape talk from feeling edges long before the names arrive.

      Sort it for real

      Raid the drawer for one spiky thing and one smooth thing.

      What it teaches

      Telling shapes apart by edges and points, not labels.

      Print it like this

      Laminate if you can; tracing fingers wear paper thin.

      Tip for today

      Trace the edge slowly with one finger and let them copy.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Match Red Flashcard for Toddlers

      One red thing up top, and a row to search below — find the other red one. This card is a colour hunt in miniature, and colour hunts are the game toddlers never seem to tire of.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Gives little eyes one clear target so the rest of the page can wait.

      Sort it for real

      Fetch the red jumper for the walk and let them spot it themselves.

      What it teaches

      Selective attention; tuning out everything that is not red.

      Print it like this

      Colours fade fast on draft mode, so pick the best setting.

      Tip for today

      Name red things in the room, then pause and let them point.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Match Blue Flashcard for Toddlers

      The same game in blue: one blue thing to match, a little row to look through. Blue is calm to look at and easy to find in most rooms, which keeps the game friendly.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Builds a patient search for one colour along one tidy row.

      Sort it for real

      Choose which blue jumper today feels like, then fetch it together.

      What it teaches

      Holding a target in mind until it turns up.

      Print it like this

      Blue ink comes out true on most home printers; check once.

      Tip for today

      If the search stalls, cover half the card with your hand.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Match Circle Flashcard for Toddlers

      Find the other circle — a shape-matching puzzle with one right answer and plenty of near-misses to talk through. Tracing with a finger makes the match much easier to see.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Sharpens round-spotting among squares and triangles pretending otherwise.

      Sort it for real

      Hunt the bathroom for anything round; sponges, soap, cotton pads.

      What it teaches

      Shape recognition that ignores size and colour distractions.

      Print it like this

      Round the corners with scissors after printing; pages feel friendlier.

      Tip for today

      Toast, buttons, clocks; circles hide in plain sight all day.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Match Triangle Flashcard for Toddlers

      One triangle to find, hiding among shapes that are almost right. Triangles are the satisfying match — three sides are easy to count on fingers together.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Teaches corner counting; three is the magic number that makes a triangle.

      Sort it for real

      Build a tall tower of blocks, then point out where the pointy corners live.

      What it teaches

      Early geometry; corners and sides as things you can count.

      Print it like this

      Card stock holds up best when corners get tapped all week.

      Tip for today

      Cheese triangles at lunch do half your teaching for you.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Sort By Color Flashcard for Toddlers

      A pile to sort into colours — the first true sorting job in the set. Your toddler groups, you name the piles, and together the muddle turns into order.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Proves that one simple rule can turn chaos into order.

      Sort it for real

      Give the peg basket a shake, then peg each colour in its own row.

      What it teaches

      Sorting by attribute; the everyday start of tidy logic.

      Print it like this

      Colour printing earns its keep here; greyscale spoils the game.

      Tip for today

      Undo one group yourself and act baffled; let the boss fix it.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Sort By Shape Flashcard for Toddlers

      Same sorting job, new rule: this time it is shapes, not colours. Switching the rule is the stretch — and noticing that the same objects can be sorted two ways is a genuinely big idea.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Replays sorting with a new rule, so flexibility becomes the habit.

      Sort it for real

      Sort the cutlery tray; all the spoons here, everything pointy over there.

      What it teaches

      Switching rules without dropping the game; flexible thinking.

      Print it like this

      Two copies print well side by side on one sheet.

      Tip for today

      Say the rule aloud at the start, then again halfway through.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Fruit Together Flashcard for Toddlers

      Fruit in one group — apples, bananas, maybe a stray vegetable sneaking in to keep everyone honest. Grouping by kind is the stepping stone from "same and different" to real categories.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Grows the habit of putting things into sensible little families.

      Sort it for real

      Make a paper-plate fruit face for pudding and name each piece as it lands.

      What it teaches

      Categories; knowing a group is more than a random pile.

      Print it like this

      Glossy photo paper makes the fruit look delicious enough to point at.

      Tip for today

      The group name matters more than any single item today.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Animals Together Flashcard for Toddlers

      Animals in one group, everything else out. This card asks your toddler to spot living things as a group — and farm visits, pets and picture books all suddenly become practice.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Shows that very different creatures can still share one group name.

      Sort it for real

      Hunt the sofa cushions for every hidden animal before lights-out.

      What it teaches

      Grouping by kind, even when members look nothing alike.

      Print it like this

      Print the sheet whole; cutting animals apart can come later.

      Tip for today

      Add animal sounds while sorting; noise makes categories memorable.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · MATCHING & SORTING · AGES 2 YEARS

      Odd One Out Flashcard for Toddlers

      Three things that belong together and one that does not — the trickiest puzzle in the set, and the most satisfying when it clicks. Spotting the stranger in the group is a big two-year-old achievement.

      Teaching tips

      What this card practises

      Sharpens noticing by sneaking in one thing that breaks the pattern.

      Sort it for real

      Set the table with three forks and one spoon and wait quietly.

      What it teaches

      Spotting rule-breakers, a thinking move grown-ups use daily.

      Print it like this

      Sturdy paper is worth it here; this card gets grabbed constantly.

      Tip for today

      Keep your face neutral while they think; surprises spoil the puzzle.

      Teach it, step by step
